print('row7 :', r7[:80])
print('row8 :', r8[:80])
print('row9 :', r9[:80])
jan=r7.index('╭January')
print('January box at col', jan, 'width', r7.index('╮',jan)-jan+1)
inner=r8[jan+1:r8.index('│',jan+1)]
print('weekday interior repr:', repr(inner))
print('M positions in interior:', [i for i,c in enumerate(inner) if c!=' '])
d=r9[jan+1:r9.index('│',jan+1)]
print('date row interior:', repr(d))
feb=r7.index('╭February')
print('February box at col', feb, 'gap between boxes:', feb-(r7.index('╮',jan)+1))
cal=strip(out[6]).index('╭2026')
print('calendar border col:', cal, 'right edge col:', strip(out[34]).index('╯'))
sec=strip(out[6]).index('╭Sections')
print('sections col:', sec, 'tags col:', strip(out[6]).index('╭Tags'))
print('menu width:', strip(out[6]).index('╮')-sec+1)
ev=[l for l in out if 'Recent' in l][0]
print('events box:', ev[:60])
print('events width:', ev.split('╮')[0])
# help line position
h=[i for i,l in enumerate(out) if 'hjkl' in l][0]
print('help row:', h, 'leading spaces:', len(strip(out[h]))-len(strip(out[h]).lstrip()))
EOF

args.command:
cat > /workspace/notes/06-log-parsing.md <<'REPORT_EOF'
# 06 — Log parsing (sections/tags) & menu behavior

Black-box findings from driving the TUI (`caps-log`, commit 93cc85d…) in a pty.
Setup: config `log-dir-path=<dir>`, log files `<dir>/y2026/d2026_08_XX.md`,
varied markdown content; screens captured at 100x40. `EDITOR=/bin/true` unless noted.
"Today" during probing was 2026-08-08.

## 1. Markdown parsing rules

### Sections
- A line becomes a section when, **after trimming leading whitespace** (spaces *and*
  tabs both work), it starts with `# ` (`#` + exactly a space) and has a non-empty
  name after trimming trailing whitespace.
  - `   # Indented Header` -> section `indented header`
  - `\t# Tabbed Header`   -> section `tabbed header`
  - `#NoSpaceSection` -> NOT a section (space after `#` required)
  - `## Double Hash`  -> NOT a section (only level-1 headers)
  - `#` alone, `#   ` (only spaces) -> NOT a section (empty name)
  - `# Trailing Space   ` -> `trailing space` (trailing spaces trimmed)
  - `# Sec: With Colon` -> `sec: with colon` (colons/parens allowed in names)
- **Case:** names are lowercased before storing/display; matching is
  case-insensitive (`# Zebra Section` and `# zebra section`, even across files,
  merge into one section `zebra section`).
- **CRLF:** section lines ending with `\r` still parse (the `\r` is trimmed).
- **First line:** by default a section header on the *first line* of a file is
  ignored (typ. the date title). With `--first-line-section` (CLI) or
  `first-line-section=true` (config; both verified) the first line participates
  like any other (`# date2` becomes section `date2`).
  Only *section headers* on line 1 are affected — a `* tag` on the first line is
  still parsed (verified: first-line tag became a root tag).

### Tags
- A line becomes a tag when, after trimming leading whitespace (`  * X` parses),
  it starts with `* ` (asterisk + space) and the rest matches the tag grammar
  (see below). Observed:
  - `* Tag Name`            -> `tag name`
  - `* Tag (info)`          -> `tag` (paren info stripped from name)
  - `* Tag (info): body`    -> `tag` (`: body` ignored)
  - `* ParenNoSpace(info)`  -> `parennospace` (`(...)` stripped even without a space before it)
  - `* ColonTag: some body` -> `colontag` (`: body` stripped even without parens)
  - `*  DoubleSpaceTag`     -> parses (multiple spaces after `*` OK)
  - `* TrailingSpaceTag   ` -> parses (trailing spaces trimmed)
  - `* MixedCase TAG Here`  -> `mixedcase tag here` (lowercased, spaces kept)
  - NOT parsed: `*NoSpaceTag`, `*\tTabbedTag` (space after `*` required),
    `- DashItem`, `+ PlusItem`, bare `*`, `* (empty tag name?)` (empty name),
    `* TagTwo(extra)more text` (trailing garbage after the `(info)` group that
    isn't `: body` invalidates the whole line).
  - **CRLF:** a tag line ending with `\r` does NOT parse at all (verified:
    `* CrlfTag\r` missing while `* LfTag` in the same file parsed). Sections
    tolerate `\r`; tags don't.
- Tag names of at least 24 chars parse fine (tested 18–24); no length limit found.
- Case-insensitive merge: `* MixedCase TAG Here` / `* mixedcase tag here` in two
  files => one tag with count 2.

### Root section
- Tags appearing before any section header in a file belong to a synthetic
  section displayed literally as `<root section>`. (Also: a first line ignored by
  the default first-line rule does NOT create a section, so tags following it
  before the next header are root tags.)
- Display string is exactly `<root section>`; it is sorted as an ordinary name
  (byte order of the lowercased string: `!bang` < `0zero` < `<root section>` <
  `zed` — verified; it is NOT pinned).

### Duplicate section within one file (quirky, verified)
- If the same section name occurs twice *in the same file*, the second occurrence
  **replaces** the earlier tag list for that file: file
  `# Sec A / * TagFirst / # Sec A / * TagSecond / # Sec B / * TagThird / # Sec A / * TagFourth`
  => Sec A has ONLY `tagfourth` (TagFirst/TagSecond vanish, even from the global
  Tags menu). Across different files, section->tags are merged (union) normally.

## 2. Menus

Layout: two boxes side by side, `╭Sections─…╮` `╭Tags─…╮`, above a
`╭Recent & upcoming events (0)─…╮` box on the left; 12-month calendar on the right;
preview box across the bottom.

- Both menus always have `<select none>` as the first entry (pinned, index 0).
- Entry format: `> ` when hovered/selected, `  ` otherwise; then for real entries
  the count right-aligned in width 3, ` │ `, then the name, space-padded:
  - `> <select none>       `
  - `    2 │ <root section> ` (i.e. `  ` + `  2` + ` │ ` + name)
  - `>   2 │ <root section>` when hovered.
  - `<select none>` has no count column.
- **Counts** = number of *distinct dates* (log files) mentioning the item, not
  number of occurrences: a tag appearing twice in one file counts 1; section
  count = number of files containing that section. Tag appearing in 2 sections of
  the same file counts 1.
- **Ordering:** strictly lexicographic on the lowercased names (verified:
  `alpha section`, `beta section`, `empty section`, `indented header`, `len
  section`, `middle section`, `section two`, `tabbed header`, `today section`,
  `trailing space`, `zebra section`). NOT insertion order.
- Long names are truncated to the box width (inner width 21 chars at 100 cols;
  e.g. `duptagintwosections` -> `duptagintwosect`, `lowercase section` ->
  `lowercase secti`). No ellipsis.
- **Scrolling:** when the list exceeds the visible height (18 rows at 100x40),
  the window follows the cursor and a heavy-line scrollbar appears on the right
  edge (`┃`, with `╻`/`╹` end caps). Observed quirk: with the menu focused and a
  too-wide selected entry, the whole menu content was shifted left by 3 columns
  (e.g. `│ 1 │ colontag` instead of `│    1 │ colontag`, selected row lost its
  `> ` prefix) — looks like FTXUI horizontal-frame behavior; with a short
  selected entry no shift occurs (`>   2 │ tagbeta       ┃`).
- Focused menu's hovered entry: `\x1b[1m\x1b[7m> <select none>        \x1b[22m\x1b[27m`
  (bold + inverted). Unfocused menu's hovered entry: `\x1b[1m\x1b[2m> …` (bold + dim).

## 3. Focus, keys, selection semantics

- Focus cycle with Tab: Sections -> Tags -> Calendar -> Sections (verified by
  focus styles; initial focus is Sections).
- `j`/`k` (and arrows) move the hovered entry in the focused menu.
- **Selection follows the cursor — Enter is NOT needed and is a no-op in menus.**
  Moving `j` onto a section/tag immediately: filters the other menu and updates
  calendar highlighting (verified without pressing Enter). Pressing Enter with a
  menu focused did nothing (sentinel `$EDITOR` script was not called).
- Selecting a section:
  - Tags menu is replaced by that section's tags only (same format/ordering;
    counts re-counted to dates where the tag appears *within that section*:
    global `tagalpha`=3 became `1` under `alpha section`).
  - Tags cursor resets to `<select none>`.
  - Calendar highlights the section's dates.
- Selecting `<select none>` in Sections: clears the section filter (Tags shows
  the full global list again, cursor reset) and clears the highlight.
- Selecting `<select none>` in Tags while a section is selected: no tag filter;

varied markdown content; screens captured at 100x40. `EDITOR=/bin/true` unless noted.

## 1. Markdown parsing rules

### Sections
- A line becomes a section when, **after trimming leading whitespace** (spaces *and*
  tabs both work), it starts with `# ` (`#` + exactly a space) and has a non-empty
  name after trimming trailing whitespace.
  - `   # Indented Header` -> section `indented header`
  - `\t# Tabbed Header`   -> section `tabbed header`
  - `#NoSpaceSection` -> NOT a section (space after `#` required)
  - `## Double Hash`  -> NOT a section (only level-1 headers)
  - `#` alone, `#   ` (only spaces) -> NOT a section (empty name)
  - `# Trailing Space   ` -> `trailing space` (trailing spaces trimmed)
  - `# Sec: With Colon` -> `sec: with colon` (colons/parens allowed in names)
- **Case:** names are lowercased before storing/display; matching is
  case-insensitive (`# Zebra Section` and `# zebra section`, even across files,
  merge into one section `zebra section`).
- **CRLF:** section lines ending with `\r` still parse (the `\r` is trimmed).
- **First line:** by default a section header on the *first line* of a file is
  ignored (typ. the date title). With `--first-line-section` (CLI) or
  `first-line-section=true` (config; both verified) the first line participates
  like any other (`# date2` becomes section `date2`).
  Only *section headers* on line 1 are affected — a `* tag` on the first line is
  still parsed (verified: first-line tag became a root tag).

### Tags
- A line becomes a tag when, after trimming leading whitespace (`  * X` parses),
  it starts with `* ` (asterisk + space) and the rest matches the tag grammar
  (see below). Observed:
  - `* Tag Name`            -> `tag name`
  - `* Tag (info)`          -> `tag` (paren info stripped from name)
  - `* Tag (info): body`    -> `tag` (`: body` ignored)
  - `* ParenNoSpace(info)`  -> `parennospace` (`(...)` stripped even without a space before it)
  - `* ColonTag: some body` -> `colontag` (`: body` stripped even without parens)
  - `*  DoubleSpaceTag`     -> parses (multiple spaces after `*` OK)
  - `* TrailingSpaceTag   ` -> parses (trailing spaces trimmed)
  - `* MixedCase TAG Here`  -> `mixedcase tag here` (lowercased, spaces kept)
  - NOT parsed: `*NoSpaceTag`, `*\tTabbedTag` (space after `*` required),
    `- DashItem`, `+ PlusItem`, bare `*`, `* (empty tag name?)` (empty name),
    `* TagTwo(extra)more text` (trailing garbage after the `(info)` group that
    isn't `: body` invalidates the whole line).
  - **CRLF:** a tag line ending with `\r` does NOT parse at all (verified:
    `* CrlfTag\r` missing while `* LfTag` in the same file parsed). Sections
    tolerate `\r`; tags don't.
- Tag names of at least 24 chars parse fine (tested 18–24); no length limit found.
- Case-insensitive merge: `* MixedCase TAG Here` / `* mixedcase tag here` in two
  files => one tag with count 2.

### Root section
- Tags appearing before any section header in a file belong to a synthetic
  section displayed literally as `<root section>`. (Also: a first line ignored by
  the default first-line rule does NOT create a section, so tags following it
  before the next header are root tags.)

  (byte order of the lowercased string: `!bang` < `0zero` < `<root section>` <
  `zed` — verified; it is NOT pinned).

  **replaces** the earlier tag list for that file: file

Report written to `/workspace/notes/06-log-parsing.md`. Summary of what was probed and found:

**Parsing rules (all verified black-box via the TUI menus):**
- **Sections**: line trimmed of leading spaces/tabs must start with `# ` (space required — `#NoSpace`, `## x`, bare `#`, `#   ` all rejected); trailing whitespace trimmed; names lowercased and merged case-insensitively across files; colons/parens allowed in names. CRLF section lines still parse.
- **Tags**: line (leading-trimmed) must start with `* ` and fully match the grammar `name [(info)] [: body]` — `* Tag (info): body` → `tag`, `* ColonTag: body` → `colontag`, `* ParenNoSpace(info)` → `parennospace`; rejected: `*NoSpace`, `*\tTab`, `- item`, `+ item`, bare `*`, `* (info)` (empty name), `* TagTwo(extra)garbage`. **CRLF tag lines don't parse at all** (asymmetry vs sections). No name length limit found (24 chars OK).
- **Root section**: literal string `<root section>`, sorted as an ordinary name (`!bang` < `0zero` < `<root section>` — not pinned).
- **First line**: only *section headers* on line 1 are ignored by default (first-line tags still parse); `--first-line-section` CLI and `first-line-section=true` config both make line 1 a normal line.
- **Quirk**: a repeated section name within one file *replaces* that section's earlier tag list for that file (tags before the repeat vanish globally).

**Menus/behavior:**
- Counts = distinct dates (files), not occurrences; ordering strictly lexicographic on lowercased names; `<select none>` pinned first; long names truncated at box width (no ellipsis); menu scrolls with a `┃` scrollbar when overflowing.
- **Selection follows the cursor — Enter is a no-op in menus**; `j` immediately filters/highlights. Tab cycle: Sections → Tags → Calendar. Selecting a section filters Tags (counts re-counted within section, cursor reset to `<select none>`); Sections `<select none>` clears filter+highlight; Tags `<select none>` falls back to section-date highlight. Enter on calendar runs `$EDITOR <full log path>`.
- **Highlight SGR** (full table in report): log date=`\x1b[4m`, weekend=`\x1b[34m`, today=`\x1b[31m`, matched section/tag=`\x1b[4m\x1b[33m` (yellow over blue; red today wins; **no distinction between section- and tag-match**); calendar cursor adds `\x1b[7m`; dates dim when calendar unfocused.
- **Preview box**: `log preview for DD. MM. YY.` (underlined title), body = raw file content, first N lines only (5 at 100x40, no scrolling observed); header lines bold+dim+yellow, tag `* ` marker bold+dim+blue, other lines plain.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Drive a program in a pty: send keys with delays, capture raw output."""
3	import os, pty, sys, time, select, fcntl, termios, struct, argparse
4	
5	def main():
6	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
7	    ap.add_argument('--cols', type=int, default=80)
8	    ap.add_argument('--rows', type=int, default=24)
9	    ap.add_argument('--out', default='/tmp/cap.raw')
10	    ap.add_argument('--settle', type=float, default=0.6, help='wait after each key')
11	    ap.add_argument('--final', type=float, default=0.8, help='wait at end')
12	    ap.add_argument('--keys', default='q', help='key specs, comma separated; \\x.. allowed')
13	    ap.add_argument('cmd', nargs=argparse.REMAINDER)
14	    a = ap.parse_args()
15	    cmd = a.cmd
16	    if cmd and cmd[0] == '--':
17	        cmd = cmd[1:]
18	
19	    pid, fd = pty.fork()
20	    if pid == 0:
21	        fcntl.ioctl(0, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack('HHHH', a.rows, a.cols, 0, 0))
22	        os.execvp(cmd[0], cmd)
23	    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack('HHHH', a.rows, a.cols, 0, 0))
24	    out = open(a.out, 'wb')
25	    def drain(dur):
26	        end = time.time() + dur
27	        while time.time() < end:
28	            r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], max(0, end - time.time()))
29	            if fd in r:
30	                try:
31	                    data = os.read(fd, 65536)
32	                except OSError:
33	                    return False
34	                if not data:
35	                    return False
36	                out.write(data)
37	                out.flush()
38	        return True
39	    drain(a.settle)
40	    keys = a.keys.split(',') if a.keys else []
41	    for k in keys:
42	        b = k.encode().decode('unicode_escape').encode('latin1')
43	        os.write(fd, b)
44	        if not drain(a.settle):
45	            break
46	    drain(a.final)
47	    out.close()
48	    try:
49	        os.kill(pid, 9)
50	    except ProcessLookupError:
51	        pass
52	    os.waitpid(pid, 0)
53

# 03 — Annual View TUI Rendering (black-box spec)

Probed `/workspace/executable` (caps-log) purely via pty captures on 2026-08-08
(today = Saturday 2026-08-08). Test log repo: `/tmp/annual/logs` with 10 files
`y2026/d2026_MM_DD.md` (01_01, 01_15, 02_03, 03_15, 03_21, 07_04, 07_18, 08_01,
08_08, 12_25) containing `# Section` headers and `* Tag` lines. Config:
`log-dir-path=/tmp/annual/logs`. All captures in `/tmp/annual/caps/*.raw`
(replay with `python3 /workspace/probe/screen.py <raw> <cols> <rows>`).

Exit code after quitting the TUI with `q`: **0**.

---

## 1. Byte-stream structure (100x40, capture cap100.raw)

### 1.1 Startup (exact bytes, offset 0)

```
\x00                                            <- literal NUL byte
\x1bP$q q\x1b\\                                 <- DCS "$q SP q" ST  (DECRQSS query of cursor style)
\x1b[?1049h                                     <- enter alternate screen
\x1b[?7l                                        <- disable auto-wrap
\x1b[?1000h \x1b[?1003h \x1b[?1015h \x1b[?1006h <- enable mouse: click, all-motion, urxvt, SGR
\x00                                            <- literal NUL flush marker
```

No `\x1b[?25l` (hide cursor) in the init; the cursor is only hidden at the END of
each rendered frame (see below). No cursor-shape set on startup.

### 1.2 First frame (starts at offset 55)

- Starts with `\r \x1b[2K` — carriage return + erase line. This is the ONLY
  `\x1b[2K` in the whole stream (checked: count = 1 in a 154 KB capture).
- Then 40 screen rows are emitted in order, top to bottom, each row padded with
  spaces to the FULL terminal width (100), rows separated by `\r\n`.
  NOTE: on a pty with ONLCR this appears on the wire as `\r\r\n` (the app's
  `\n` is expanded to `\r\n` by the pty). The last row has no trailing newline.
- Frame ends with a cursor park + hide + flush:
  `\x1b[37A\x1b[77D \x1b[?25l \x00`  (37 rows up, 77 cols left, hide cursor, NUL).
  With the Sections menu focused the cursor is parked at (row 2, col 22) — the
  cell right after the inverted `> <select none>` entry.

### 1.3 Subsequent frames (each ~8110 bytes at 100x40)

The app redraws the ENTIRE screen continuously (a 5 s capture contained 19 full
frames even with no input). Frame N>1 structure:

```
\x1b[37B\x1b[77C      <- undo previous frame's cursor park
\r                    <- column 0
\x1b[1A  (x39)        <- move to top row: (rows-1) individual CUU sequences, NOT one "\x1b[39A"
<40 full-width rows, separated by \r\n; no \x1b[2K, no clear-screen>
\x1b[37A\x1b[77D \x1b[?25l \x00
```

Every row is always rewritten with full-width space padding — there is no diff
optimization. A trailing `\x00` byte is written after every frame (flush marker).

Cursor park depends on focus (format `\x1b[<up>A\x1b[<left>D` from bottom-right):
- Sections menu focused: `\x1b[37A\x1b[77D`  → (2,22), end of Sections selected entry
- Tags menu focused (1 Tab): `\x1b[37A\x1b[52D` → (2,47), end of Tags selected entry
- Calendar focused (2 Tabs): `\x1b[23A\x1b[22D` → (16,77), inside the August box
  (inexact cell position; cursor is hidden anyway)
The next frame opens with the matching `\x1b[<n>B\x1b[<m>C`.

### 1.4 Teardown (after pressing `q`, exact tail bytes)

```
\x1b[37B\x1b[77C                          <- undo last cursor park
\x1b[?1006l \x1b[?1015l \x1b[?1003l \x1b[?1000l   <- mouse modes off (reverse order of enable)
\x1b[?7h                                  <- re-enable auto-wrap
\x1b[?1049l                               <- leave alternate screen
\x1b[?25h                                 <- show cursor
\x1b[1 q                                  <- DECSCUSR: blinking block cursor (note the space before q)
\x00                                      <- flush NUL
\r                                        <- lone carriage return (last byte)
```

`\x1b[?25h` occurs exactly once in the stream. Process then exits 0.

---

## 2. Screen layout (reference: 100x40, cap100.raw)

```
00|                 Today is: 08. 08. 2026.  | There are 10 log entries for year 2026.
01|╭Sections───────────────╮╭Tags───────────────────╮╭2026──────────────────┬┬─────────────────────┬╮
02|│> <select none>        ││> <select none>        │││23 24 25 26 27 28 29 ││27 28 29 30          ││
03|│    1 │ birthday       ││    1 │ beware         │││30 31                ││                     ││
04|│    1 │ christmas      ││    1 │ coding         ││╰─────────────────────╯╰─────────────────────╯│
05|│    2 │ health         ││    1 │ coffee         ││╭May──────────────────╮╭June─────────────────╮│
... (menus)                                                      (months, 2 per row)
20|╰───────────────────────╯╰───────────────────────╯││                     ││31                   ││
21|╭Recent & upcoming events (0)────────────────────╮│╰─────────────────────╯╰─────────────────────╯│
22|╰────────────────────────────────────────────────╯│╭September────────────╮╭October──────────────╮│
...
31|                                                  ╰──────────────────────────────────────────────╯
32|╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
33|│                                   log preview for 08. 08. 26.                                    │
34|│# 2026-08-08                                                                                      │
...
39|╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

Vertical stack: (1) info line; (2) main area = [menu column | calendar];
(3) log preview box; (4) help line (only when it fits, §6).
Menu column = Sections box + Tags box stacked, then the events box below them.
Calendar is a bordered box with the year as border title; month boxes inside.

### 2.1 Geometry (all chars are single-width)

- Menu boxes: 25 wide (`╭Sections` + dashes + `╮`). Interior 23.
  - Selected entry: `> <select none>` left-aligned, padded to 21.
  - Normal entry: `    1 │ birthday       ` = 4 spaces, count, ` │ `, name
    (lowercased), padded. Count = number of log files mentioning it.
    Both menus are sorted alphabetically; `<select none>` pinned on top.
- Month box: **23 wide × 9 tall** (interior 21 = 7 columns × 3).
  - Title row: `╭January──────────────╮` — name right after `╭`, rest filled
    with `─` (left-aligned, NOT centered). Same for the calendar's `╭2026──╮`
    and all box titles.
  - Weekday header row: ` M  T  W  T  F  S  S ` — letters at interior columns
    1,4,7,10,13,16,19 (Monday first by default; with `sunday-start=true` it is
    ` S  M  T  W  T  F  S `).
  - 6 week rows always (empty trailing weeks stay blank). Each date is
    right-aligned in a 2-char field ending at its weekday column, followed by
    one space: e.g. `       1  2  3  4  5 `, ` 5  6  7  8  9 10 11 `.
    Non-day cells are spaces.
- Month boxes in a row are directly adjacent (gap 0): `...╮╭...`.
- Events box: width = both menus (50). Height = 2 + entries (0 events → 2 rows,
  borders only). Title `Recent & upcoming events (N)`.
- Preview box: full terminal width when the layout doesn't fit horizontally;
  height = remaining rows.

### 2.2 Info line (row 0)

`Today is: 08. 08. 2026.  | There are 10 log entries for year 2026.`
- Format: `Today is: DD. MM. YYYY.` (space after each dot, trailing dot), then
  TWO spaces, `| `, then `There are N log entries for year YYYY.`
- **No singular handling**: with exactly one log it prints
  `There are 1 log entries for year 2026.` (verified). With 0 logs (year
  changed with `+`): `There are 0 log entries for year 2027.`
- Centered horizontally: at 100 cols, 17 leading + 17 trailing spaces
  (text is 66 chars). Style: bold + underlined (`\x1b[1m\x1b[4m` … `\x1b[22m\x1b[24m`).
- If the terminal is narrower than the text it is left-clipped (no centering
  possible): at 60 cols row 0 shows the first 60 chars only.

### 2.3 Preview box

- Title: `log preview for 08. 08. 26.` — format `DD. MM. YY.` (2-digit year,
  spaces after dots, trailing dot), centered inside the box, underlined; the
  whole title row is bold (FTXUI window title) + dim when unfocused:
  `│\x1b[1m\x1b[2m <pad> \x1b[4m log preview for 08. 08. 26. \x1b[24m <pad> \x1b[22m\x1b[2m│`.
- Body: the raw markdown log for the selected date, first line included
  (first line is only ignored for section detection). Follows selection as the
  calendar cursor moves (`l` → `log preview for 09. 08. 26.` with empty body
  for a missing log).

---

## 3. Exact SGR sequences (default theme)

The app uses "focus dimming": every component EXCEPT the focused one is dim
(`\x1b[2m`). Startup focus = Sections menu. Tab cycles
Sections → Tags → Calendar → (back). Dim is toggled per line with `\x1b[2m` /
`\x1b[22m` pairs, e.g. a row with focus on Sections:

```
│\x1b[1m\x1b[7m> <select none>       \x1b[22m\x1b[27m │\x1b[2m│\x1b[1m\x1b[2m> <select none>       \x1b[22m\x1b[2m │││23 24 ... \x1b[22m
```

- Focused menu selected entry: bold + inverted = `\x1b[1m\x1b[7m … \x1b[22m\x1b[27m`
- Unfocused menu selected entry: bold + dim = `\x1b[1m\x1b[2m … \x1b[22m\x1b[2m`
- Info line: `\x1b[1m\x1b[4m … \x1b[22m\x1b[24m` (bold, underlined)
- Weekday header ` M  T  W  T  F  S  S `: `\x1b[4m … \x1b[24m` (underlined)

`\x1b[49m` before/after; foreground reset `\x1b[39m`; underline off `\x1b[24m`):

| date kind                       | SGR (calendar focused)                | meaning |
|---------------------------------|---------------------------------------|---------|
| empty weekday                   | `\x1b[2m 23 \x1b[22m`                 | dim |
| empty weekend                   | `\x1b[2m\x1b[34m\x1b[49m 9 \x1b[22m\x1b[39m\x1b[49m` | dim + blue(34) |

| today (no log)                  | `\x1b[2m\x1b[31m\x1b[49m 8 …`         | dim + red(31) |
| today (has log, also Saturday)  | `\x1b[4m\x1b[31m\x1b[49m 8 \x1b[24m\x1b[39m\x1b[49m`  | underline + red |

# 02 — Config File (INI) Parsing Behavior

Binary: `/workspace/executable` (caps-log, `commit-93cc85d16ab60ba8d646458fe0233778317b22a3`).
All probes black-box. HOME=`/opt/uiuc-agent/home`. "TUI launches" below = process prints the
FTXUI init sequence (`\x1b[?1049h\x1b[?7l\x1b[?1000h\x1b[?1003h\x1b[?1015h\x1b[?1006h` …) and runs
until SIGKILLed (exit 137 under `timeout -s KILL 2`); that is the success path.

## Error envelope (all failures)

Errors go to **stdout**, exit code **1**. Exact bytes (od -c verified):

```
Captain's log encountered an error: \n <message>\n
```

i.e. literal `Captain's log encountered an error: ` (trailing space), `\n`, one space, then the
message, then `\n`. Example: `Captain's log encountered an error: \n Password provided for a non encrypted repository!\n`.

## Validation order (determined by pairing two bad settings)

1. Config file open (`Failed to open file: …`)
2. INI syntax parse (`Failed to parse configuration file: …`)
3. `[calendar-events]` entries (`No such node (name|date)`, `Invalid date format: …`)
4. `[view…]` theme colors/borders (`Invalid …`)
5. `log-dir-path` emptiness (`Log directory path can not be empty!`)
6. `[git]` validation (see order below)
7. Filesystem ops on log dir (mkdir / `filesystem error: …`), then encryption/password checks

Evidence: bad event date beat bad theme color, empty log-dir and git errors; bad theme beat
empty log-dir and git errors; empty log-dir beat git errors; git errors beat mkdir filesystem errors.

## Config file location / opening

- Default path: `$HOME/.caps-log/config.ini` (`/opt/uiuc-agent/home/.caps-log/config.ini` here).
  Missing → `Failed to open file: /opt/uiuc-agent/home/.caps-log/config.ini`, exit 1. **A config
  file is mandatory even when all options come from CLI.**
- `-c <missing>` → `Failed to open file: <path>`, exit 1.
- `-c <directory>` → `basic_filebuf::underflow error reading the file: Is a directory`, exit 1.

## INI syntax (parser behaves like Boost property_tree `read_ini`)

- Empty config file → OK, launches TUI with all defaults.
- Unknown top-level keys (e.g. `unknown-key=foo`) → **silently ignored**, TUI launches.
- Unknown sections (e.g. `[unknownsection]`) → **silently ignored**.
- Line with no `=` → `Failed to parse configuration file: <unspecified file>(N): '=' character not found in line`, exit 1 (N = 1-based line number; note literal `<unspecified file>`).
- Unclosed section header `[bad header` → `Failed to parse configuration file: <unspecified file>(N): unmatched '['`, exit 1.
- Duplicate key (same section) → `Failed to parse configuration file: <unspecified file>(N): duplicate key name`, exit 1.
- Comments: both `# …` and `; …` full-line comments accepted.
- Whitespace around key and value is trimmed: `  log-dir-path  =   /tmp/x   ` works; the directory
  created is `/tmp/x` (no trailing spaces). Inner spaces of values are kept.
- **Quotes are NOT stripped**: `log-dir-path="/tmp/x"` makes the app create/use a directory
  literally named `"/tmp/x"` (relative, since it starts with `"`). Same for single quotes.
- Keys are **case-sensitive**: `Log-Dir-Path=…` is ignored (app fell back to default log dir —
  verified: screen showed "There are 0 log entries" while the intended dir had 1).

## Top-level (root section) keys

Recognized: `log-dir-path`, `log-filename-format`, `sunday-start`, `first-line-section`, `password`.
Everything else at root is ignored.

- **`log-name-format` is NOT a config key** (CLI-only). Config with `log-name-format=d%Y-%m-%d.txt`
  still created `y2026/d2026_08_08.md`. The ini key is `log-filename-format` (as in README ini
  sample): with `log-filename-format=d%Y-%m-%d.txt`, opening today's entry invoked
  `$EDITOR /tmp/…/y2026/d2026-08-08.txt`. The year subdirectory is always `y%Y` (`y2026`)
  regardless of the filename format.
- `log-filename-format` with a bad strftime spec (`d%Q.md`) → no error, TUI launches.
- **Booleans** (`sunday-start`, `first-line-section`, `enable-git-log-repo`, theme style flags):
  only exact lowercase `true` and `1` are truthy. `false`, `0`, `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`,
  `TRUE`, `True`, `invalid`, empty → all falsy. **No error on any value.**
  Verified behaviorally: `sunday-start=true`/`1` → month header ` S  M  T  W  T  F  S `;
  all others → ` M  T  W  T  F  S  S `. `first-line-section=true`/`1` → first line of the log
  (`# FirstLineSec`) appears in the Sections menu; other values → first line ignored.
- `log-dir-path=` (empty) → `Log directory path can not be empty!`, exit 1.
- `log-dir-path=~/x` → **`~` expands to $HOME** (dir `/opt/uiuc-agent/home/x` was created).
- `log-dir-path=relativedir` → relative to the process **CWD** (dir created under cwd).
- `log-dir-path` pointing at an existing regular file →
  `filesystem error: cannot create directories: Not a directory [/tmp/cfgprobe/afile]`, exit 1.
- `log-dir-path` under a regular file (`/tmp/…/afile/sub`) → same `Not a directory` message.
- `log-dir-path=/proc/x` (uncreatable) →
  `filesystem error: cannot create directories: No such file or directory [/proc/cfgprobe-cantcreate]`, exit 1.
- Unreadable (chmod 000) dir → launched fine **but we run as root**, so perms were bypassed;
  could not probe a genuine EACCES.
- `password=` (empty) → treated as "no password", TUI launches.
- `password=secretpw` on a non-encrypted log dir (no `.cle` marker) →
  `Password provided for a non encrypted repository!`, exit 1.
- CLI flags override config: `-c cfg` (with `log-dir-path=A`) plus `--log-dir-path B` →
  editor invoked on `B/y2026/d2026_08_08.md`.

## `[git]` section

- `enable-git-log-repo=false`, any invalid value, or key absent → **all other `[git]` keys are
  ignored**, TUI launches (even with bogus `ssh-key-path` present).
- Git keys at root level (no `[git]` header) are ignored.
- When enabled, validation fires in this exact order (each exit 1):
  1. `SSH key path can not be empty!`            (ssh-key-path missing/empty)
  2. `SSH public key path can not be empty!`     (ssh-pub-key-path missing/empty)
  3. `Git repository root can not be empty!`     (repo-root missing/empty)
  4. `Error! Git repo root (<repo-root>) is not parent of log dir (<log-dir>)!`
     — containment check runs **before** any existence checks. `repo-root == log-dir-path`
     passes (non-strict prefix).
  5. `SSH key does not exist: <path>`            (private key file missing)
  6. `SSH public key does not exist: <path>`     (pub key file missing)
  7. `Git repository root does not exist: <path>`(repo-root dir missing)
  8. Repo-root exists but is not a git repo → two-line message:
     `Git error @/workspace/source/utils/git_repo.cpp:95\n\tcould not find repository from '/tmp/cfgprobe/repo'`
     (second line is TAB-indented; leaks a build-machine source path).
- A valid `git init`'ed repo-root **without any remote** → TUI launches fine (remote is only
  touched on exit push/pull, not validated at startup).
- `remote-name`, `main-branch-name` not probed further (defaults origin/master per README).

## `[calendar-events]` section

- Structure: `[calendar-events.<group>.<N>]` with `name` and `date` keys. `<group>` is free-form —
  `[calendar-events.random.0]` accepted and displayed under its own heading (`birthdays`,
  `holidays` are just example names).
- Missing `name` → `No such node (name)`, exit 1. Missing `date` → `No such node (date)`, exit 1.
  Both missing → `name` error first. Empty `name=` → accepted.
- Date format: `D.M.` — day and month as 1–2 digit numbers; trailing dot optional
  (`18.07` and `18.07.` both OK); single digits OK (`1.1.`); **no range validation**
  (`32.01.`, `00.00.` accepted!); trailing garbage after second dot tolerated (`18.07.2026` OK).

# 08 — Date format, filename generation/parsing, calendar & year navigation

Probed black-box on `/workspace/executable` (version banner: `commit-93cc85d16ab60ba8d646458fe0233778317b22a3`).
System date during probing: **Sat 2026-08-08 (UTC)**. HOME=/opt/uiuc-agent/home.
All TUI runs used the pty harness; log creation used `EDITOR=<script that appends "X\n">`.

## 0. TUI basics needed to reproduce anything

- Initial keyboard focus is on the **Sections menu**, NOT the calendar. Focus order with `Tab`:
  Sections → Tags → Calendar. The focused menu's selected row is drawn inverted (`\x1b[7m`).
  Until the calendar is focused, `hjkl`/arrows/Enter do nothing to dates.
- `+` / `-` (year nav) work from ANY focus (global keys).
- `q` quits (exit 0). The TUI ignores SIGTERM.
- At startup only `<log-dir>/scratchpads/` is created. `y<year>/` is created lazily the first
  time a log is opened for that year (the dir stays even if the file ends up deleted).

## 1. Filename generation (what file is created for a date)

Config key is `log-filename-format` (README name). CLI flag is `--log-name-format` (note:
**name**, not "filename"; the help text has no defaults printed). CLI overrides config.
CLI `--log-name-format` and config `log-filename-format` both confirmed working.

**The compiled-in default is NOT the README's `d%y_%m_%d.md`.** With no option, opening
today's log creates `<log-dir>/y2026/d2026_08_08.md` (4-digit year), so the real default
behaves like `d%Y_%m_%d.md`. Passing `d%y_%m_%d.md` explicitly yields `d26_08_08.md`.

Observed generations for date 2026-08-08 (format → file created under `y2026/`):

| format | created file |
|---|---|
| (default) | `d2026_08_08.md` |
| `d%y_%m_%d.md` | `d26_08_08.md` |
| `%Y_%m_%d.md` | `2026_08_08.md` |
| `%y-%m-%d.md` | `26-08-08.md` |
| `%m.md` | `08.md` |
| `%d.md` | `08.md` |
| `%e.md` | `␣8.md` (space-padded day) |
| `%B.md` | `August.md` |
| `%b.md` | `Aug.md` |
| `%H.md` | `00.md` (time fields are always 0) |
| `%p_%I.md` | `AM_12.md` |
| `%j.md` | `001.md` (day-of-year is NOT computed; tm_yday stays 0) |
| `%A.md` | `Sunday.md` (weekday NOT computed; tm_wday stays 0 — 2026-08-08 is actually Saturday) |
| `%a_%w.md` | `Sun_0.md` |
| `%F.md` | `2026-08-08.md` (composites of Y/m/d work) |
| `a%%b.md` | `a%b.md` |
| `plain.md` | `plain.md` (no specifiers → constant name) |
| `%Q.md` | `%Q.md` (unknown specifiers pass through literally, NO error) |
| `x%.md` | `x%.md` (trailing `%` stays literal, NO error) |
| `d%y_%m_%d_%Q.md` | `d26_08_08_%Q.md` |
| `%m/%d.md` | `y2026/08/08.md` — slashes in the format create nested subdirs |

Conclusion: generation is a plain strftime over a `struct tm` that has ONLY
year/month/mday populated (wday, yday, hour, min, sec all zero). Everything strftime
accepts "works"; unknown/convenience specifiers behave per libc.

### Empty format is the only rejected format

`--log-name-format ''` (or empty config value) aborts at startup, before any directory
is created (not even `scratchpads/`), printing to stdout (exit code 1):

```
Captain's log encountered an error: 
 Log filename format can not be empty!
```

Exact bytes (piped): `Captain's log encountered an error: \n Log filename format can not be empty!\n\t`
— note the space after `error: `, the leading space before `Log`, and a trailing TAB after `!`.

## 2. The log file lifecycle (Enter on a date)

1. App ensures `y<year>/` exists, creates `<log-dir>/y<YYYY>/<formatted-name>` with the
   template content, then runs `$EDITOR <path>` (via shell).

import os, pty, sys, time, select, fcntl, termios, struct
rows, cols = 40, 100

    while time.time()<end:

            try: data=os.read(fd,65536)

Report written to `/workspace/notes/08-date-format.md`. Key findings:

**Filename generation**
- Real default format behaves like `d%Y_%m_%d.md` (README's `d%y_%m_%d.md` is wrong — `%y` gives 2-digit years: `d26_08_08.md`).
- Generation is plain strftime over a `tm` with only year/month/mday set: `%H`→`00`, `%j`→`001`, `%A`→`Sunday` (always), `%F` works, `%e`→space-padded, `%B`→`August`, `%%`→`%`.
- Unknown specifiers (`%Q`, trailing `%`) pass through literally, no error. Slashes in format create nested dirs (`%m/%d.md` → `y2026/08/08.md`). Only rejected format is empty: `Captain's log encountered an error: \n Log filename format can not be empty!\n\t`, exit 1.
- CLI is `--log-name-format`, config key is `log-filename-format`; CLI wins.

**Log lifecycle**
- File created at `yYYYY/<name>` with 12-byte template `# %d. %m. %y.` (no trailing newline), then `$EDITOR` runs; if content is byte-identical after the editor exits, the file is **deleted** (content-based, not mtime). `y<year>/` is created lazily on first open; only `scratchpads/` is made at startup.

**Counting/parsing (TUI)**
- `There are N log entries for year X.` = number of days of year X whose *generated* filename exists in `yX/` (no singular form). Generation-based, so: root files ignored, only `y\d{4}` dirs scanned, scratchpads/other/nested dirs ignored, impossible dates (Feb 30, month 13) and mismatched dir/name years never count, single-digit-month names don't match. Format `plain.md` → 365; `%m.md` with `08.md` → 31. Tags/sections menus follow the same rule. Log dates render underlined; today red; weekends blue.
- `--encrypt` instead uses a lenient full-name strptime parse: single-digit month/day accepted, month 1–12, day 1–31, Feb 30 accepted, trailing junk rejected; also encrypts all `scratchpads/*.md`; root files untouched.

**Calendar/navigation**
- Focus starts on Sections menu (Tab: Sections→Tags→Calendar); `+`/`-` are global, keep cursor month/day, preview title follows (`log preview for %d. %m. %y.`). Initial year = system-clock year. `--sunday-start`/`sunday-start=true` changes header ` M  T  W  T  F  S  S` → ` S  M  T  W  T  F  S`. `r` had no observable effect. Top bar: `Today is: %d. %m. %Y.` (never changes) + count segment.
